title: Loans, savings, remittances: find the true cost and the risk
course_title: Fintech Fundamentals: How Digital Finance Works in Africa

say: Loans, savings and remittances: find the true cost, and the risk.
This is the video for module two of Fintech Fundamentals.
A digital loan can let a trader restock today instead of next month. But some apps charged very high fees and harassed borrowers.

say: Savings and remittance products touch two of the most important money flows in a household. Both are full of fine print.

say: And if customers fear losing money, they go back to cash. In fintech, trust is the product.

say: Loan apps often show a fee or a total to repay, not a rate. To compare fairly, turn every loan into a rate for the same period. For example, Bisi in Ibadan needs 50,000 naira for stock.

card.title: Bisi compares two loan offers
card.note: Turn every loan into a monthly rate first.

say: App A says repay 57,500 naira in 30 days. The cost is 7,500 naira, which is 15% a month, or about 182.5% a year.

card.title: Bisi compares two loan offers
card.note: Turn every loan into a monthly rate first.

say: App B says repay 62,000 naira over 3 months. The cost is 12,000 naira, about 8% a month.
Her stock earns about 10,000 naira per cycle, so App A's cost eats 75% of one cycle's profit. The cheaper-looking short loan is the more expensive one.

rows: App B cost: about 8% a month

say: The FCCPC supervises digital consumer lenders and publishes the list of approved ones. A responsible lender shows the full cost before you accept, and starts small.

panel.heading: Responsible lender or predatory app?
left: Full cost shown before you accept
right: Hides the total until paid out
Pushes a new loan to repay old

say: Red flags: an app that demands your contacts or photos, threatens to message your family, which regulators have prohibited, hides the total, or pushes a new loan to repay the old one.

say: Before you save in an app, know what you own. A bank deposit is regulated by the CBN and insured by the NDIC up to a limit. Look up the current limit on the NDIC website.

cards.d: Regulated by the CBN. NDIC deposit insurance up to a limit. Check the current limit yourself.
A claim on float held at banks. Protected by float safeguarding rules.
For example a money market fund. Regulated by SEC Nigeria. Its value can go up or down.

say: A wallet balance is a claim on float that must be held at banks.

cards.d: Regulated by the CBN. NDIC deposit insurance up to a limit. Check the current limit yourself.

For example a money market fund. Regulated by SEC Nigeria. Its value can go up or down.

say: An investment, such as a money market fund, is regulated by SEC Nigeria, and its value can go down. So the words guaranteed returns on an investment are a warning sign.

say: A remittance charges you twice: an upfront fee, and an exchange-rate margin, the gap between your rate and the mid-market rate. The margin is often bigger, and easy to miss.

panel.heading: Zero fees is not the same as cheapest
items: A: zero fees, mother gets 388,000 naira
B: 3 pound fee, mother gets 398,000 naira
Compare what the recipient finally gets

say: For example, Ngozi in Manchester sends 200 pounds to her mother in Enugu. Provider A advertises zero fees, and her mother receives 388,000 naira. That costs 3%.

panel.heading: Zero fees is not the same as cheapest
items: A: zero fees, mother gets 388,000 naira
B: 3 pound fee, mother gets 398,000 naira
Compare what the recipient finally gets

say: Provider B charges a 3 pound fee but gives a better rate, and her mother receives 398,000 naira, at about 2%. So always compare what the recipient finally gets. And use licensed channels only, never social media forex sellers.

say: In a SIM swap, a fraudster gets a new SIM on your number and receives your OTPs. In social engineering, a caller pretends to be the bank and asks for your PIN, OTP or BVN.

panel.heading: The fraud types you must recognise
items: SIM swap: a new SIM on your number
Account takeover: stolen phone or password

say: Account takeover uses stolen passwords or phones. Money mules are accounts rented to receive and move stolen money.

panel.heading: The fraud types you must recognise
items: SIM swap: a new SIM on your number
Account takeover: stolen phone or password

say: And fake platforms promise high fixed returns, pay early members from new deposits, then collapse. Check licences with the SEC or CBN.

panel.heading: The fraud types you must recognise
items: SIM swap: a new SIM on your number
Account takeover: stolen phone or password

say: For example, Kemi got a call from the bank, she thought, and read out an OTP. At 9:02 am, 85,000 naira left her wallet.
At 9:10 am she calls the wallet's support line. Speed is everything. The first minutes decide whether funds can be frozen.
The agent blocks her wallet, and the fraud team asks the receiving bank to hold the beneficiary account.
Kemi files a police report and keeps every reference number. If unsatisfied, she can escalate to the CBN's consumer protection department or the FCCPC.
Remember this rule. No genuine bank, wallet or regulator will ever ask for your PIN, password or OTP. If anyone does, end the call, and contact your provider through the number in its official app.

panel.heading: Kemi reports a fraud fast
panel.rule: No genuine bank will ever ask for your PIN, password or OTP.

say: To remember. Compare loans by monthly rate. Check that a lender is on the FCCPC list. Know whether your savings are a deposit, a wallet or an investment. Add the fee and the exchange margin together. And never share your PIN or OTP.

items: Check the FCCPC approved lenders list
